name: LNK
reason: Routing references is simple; electrical loading would need a separate optional model.

name: MLT
reason: Easy fan-out and normalled connections; little need for this many duplicate ports in software.

name: P
reason: Simple arithmetic. Preserve its intended low-frequency control behavior.

name: PAB
reason: Fractional raster-sample delays can reproduce registration shifts; timing and interpolation matter.

name: PGO
reason: Straightforward signed arithmetic with configurable routing and clipping.

name: PRM
reason: Direct mathematical operators; feedback-patched division needs the shared loop solver.

name: Angles
reason: Compute horizontal/vertical coordinates and fixed-angle mixtures directly.

name: Contour
reason: Needs filters running in raster order, including history across lines, for convincing streaks.

name: DC Distro 3A
reason: No signal-processing function to recreate in Rack.

name: DSG3
reason: Folds, curves, min/max and blends map well to per-pixel processing.

name: DWO3
reason: Free-running phase, reset, sync, and video-rate FM require time-aware synthesis.

name: ESG3
reason: Virtual timing and composite encoding are feasible. Electrical output and genlock require hardware.

name: Factors
reason: Multiplication around a defined midpoint maps directly to software.

name: FKG3
reason: Per-pixel comparisons, soft transitions and RGB interpolation are straightforward.

name: Keychain
reason: Threshold comparisons are easy; exact edge speed and tiny delays require oversampling.

name: Matte
reason: Constant fields and averages are elementary; retain its averaging behavior.

name: Proc
reason: Signed values and operation order must be preserved before final display clipping.

name: Ribbons
reason: Straightforward thresholds and bit outputs. Avoid adding an artificial pixelation clock.

name: Scrolls
reason: Feasible stateful motion engine; reproduce modes, slew and timing rather than only translating a texture.

name: SMX3
reason: Small per-pixel matrix operations; preserve negative and above-white intermediate values.

name: Stacker
reason: Comparisons and priority masks are inexpensive GPU operations.

name: Stairs
reason: Piecewise transfer curves are easy; fine patterns need controlled antialiasing.

name: Sum/Dist
reason: Simple adds and routing. Optional propagation-delay modeling would raise fidelity effort.

name: Swatch
reason: Matrix transforms are straightforward; preserve unclamped outputs where appropriate.

name: Switcher
reason: Per-pixel selection supports image-controlled switching as well as ordinary CV selection.

name: TBC2
reason: File/camera ingestion and frame synchronization are feasible; raw analog decoding depends on capture hardware.

name: TBC2 Expander
reason: Physical connector breakout; represent supported inputs in the software input module.

name: Castle 000 ADC
reason: Thresholds generate bit planes; analog edge characteristics are a separate fidelity layer.

name: Castle 001 DAC
reason: Weighted sums of bit planes are easy.

name: Castle 010 Clock VCO
reason: Must resolve clock edges at video time scales independently of Rack's audio rate.

name: Castle 011 Shift Register
reason: State must advance in raster-time order, not once per display frame.

name: Castle 100 Multi Gate
reason: Direct boolean operations after the input thresholds.

name: Castle 101 Quad Gate
reason: Small truth tables and routing; chip variants can become selectable modes.

name: Castle 110 Counter
reason: Simple state logic, but arbitrary video clocks require edge-accurate evaluation.

name: Castle 111 D Flip Flops
reason: Sampling, reset and state history need a defined timing model.

name: Diver
reason: Capture an audio buffer and read it along raster axes; freeze and phase behavior need careful timing.

name: Escher Sketch
reason: XY and gesture recording are easy; pressure and the physical feel depend on the input device.

name: Fortress
reason: Counters, bit operations, shift registers and cellular automata are implementable; slip-sync is the harder part.

name: Memory Palace
reason: Strong candidate. Delay buffers, transforms, keying and painting are standard techniques, but integration is substantial.

name: Arch
reason: Min/max, rectification and transfer curves map directly to GPU arithmetic.

name: Bridge
reason: Simple operations; video ports and ordinary Rack CV still need explicit conversion.

name: Color Chords
reason: Layer opacity and priority are straightforward to implement.

name: Curtain
reason: Model raster-time filter response, rectification and wet/dry mixing for its characteristic trails.

name: Cyclops
reason: An onscreen vector preview is easy; actual ILDA output needs a compatible DAC and separate integration.

name: Doorway
reason: Gain, clipping, rectification and foreground/background blending are direct operations.

name: Liquid TV
reason: An embedded monitor is straightforward; physical display electronics add no necessary software behavior.

name: Mapper
reason: Implement its color mapping and transfer curves; do not substitute a generic HSV picker without checking behavior.

name: Marble Index
reason: All operations are feasible; numerous routing, inversion and solarization combinations require careful reconstruction.

name: Navigator
reason: Arithmetic on two signal fields; it does not require a general 3D renderer.

name: Passage
reason: Basic gain, inversion, offset and mixing; preserve the documented operation order.

name: Pendulum
reason: LFOs, crossfading and routing fit Rack naturally; response curves need calibration.

name: Polar Fringe
reason: Feasible color-distance/transfer model; matching the hardware's soft boundary needs references.

name: Prismatic Ray
reason: Same timing challenges as DWO3: free phase, modulation, reset and alias control.

name: Sensory Translator
reason: Audio filters and envelope followers are native DSP tasks; route Mac microphone through an audio input.

name: Shapechanger
reason: Feasible nonlinear math, with work needed to recover exact curves and control interactions.

name: Staircase
reason: Piecewise waveshaping is inexpensive; preserve continuous folds rather than imposing stepped posterization.

name: Topogram
reason: Threshold bands, edge softness and grouped outputs are direct per-pixel operations.

name: Visual Cortex
reason: Its generator, colorizer and compositor translate well; encoder/decoder and timing add integration work.

name: War Of The Ants
reason: Model correlated noise across raster time and motion, not independent random pixels alone.

name: Cadet I Sync Generator
reason: Virtual timing is straightforward; reproducing lock behavior and actual electrical sync is harder.

name: Cadet II RGB Encoder
reason: Shares the NTSC encoder engine; real composite output needs hardware.

name: Cadet III Video Input
reason: Virtual clamping/conditioning is feasible; physical signal recovery depends on the input interface.

name: Cadet IV Dual Ramp Generator
reason: Deterministic coordinate fields with defined reset and blanking.

name: Cadet IX VCO
reason: Requires video-time phase integration and sync modeling.

name: Cadet V Scaler
reason: Small fixed gain/offset operators; build variants can be modes.

name: Cadet VI Fader
reason: Direct interpolation with the appropriate control range.

name: Cadet VII Processor
reason: Simple gain/offset/summing primitives; verify exact circuit routing before implementation.

name: Cadet VIII Hard Key Generator
reason: Direct thresholds, with edge modeling available later.

name: Cadet X Multiplier
reason: Direct arithmetic with the appropriate sign and clipping conventions.

name: Colorspace Mapper
reason: Recover documented color mapping rather than assuming standard HSV behavior.

name: Differentiator
reason: A raster-time filter is feasible; exact response needs a more complete circuit audit.

name: Function Generator
reason: Piecewise transfer functions fit software well; confirm the production revision's response.

name: Triple Video Fader & Key Generator
reason: Comparisons and blends are easy; retain normalled connections and mode logic.

name: Triple Video Interface
reason: Virtual processing is feasible; external voltages and genlock require hardware.

name: Triple Video Processor
reason: Order of operations is significant and must match the original.

name: Video Blending Matrix
reason: Simple sums and absolute-value processing.

name: Video Flip Flops
reason: Needs raster-clock state, not frame-only evaluation.

name: Video Logic
reason: Truth tables are easy; hardware edge artifacts need extra modeling.

name: Video Waveform Generator
reason: Stable sync and modulation require the shared time-domain oscillator engine.

name: Voltage Interface I
reason: Gain, offset and clipping are simple; physical voltage output remains external.

name: Audio Frequency Decoder
reason: Ordinary audio DSP; filter constants need matching.

name: Color Time Base Corrector
reason: Virtual frame alignment is practical; physical decoding needs capture hardware.

name: Color Video Encoder
reason: Shares the NTSC engine; electrical output is separate.

name: Octal Video Quantizer & Sequencer
reason: The arithmetic is easy; clock ordering needs care.

name: Triple Video Multimode Filter
reason: Preserve raster-time state and response curves.

name: Video Divisions
reason: Needs the shared edge-timing engine.

name: Video Ramps
reason: Straightforward coordinate arithmetic.

name: Video Sync Generator
reason: Virtual timing is feasible; physical locking is separate.

name: Voltage Bridge
reason: Straightforward gain operators.

name: XY Display Driver
reason: Virtual preview is feasible; hardware behavior is sparsely documented.

name: DC Distro 5A
reason: Hardware power utility; no software processing role.

name: Chromagnon
reason: Shape/color processing is feasible; evolving revisions complicate exact matching. Physical ILDA and analog I/O need hardware.

name: Videomancer
reason: Feasible program by program. Public VHDL examples help, but FPGA programs must be translated; they are not Rack binaries.

name: Vidiot
reason: Build from oscillator, keyer, color and input engines; interaction and feedback require tuning.

name: BitVision
reason: Pixel graphics and audio modulation are easy; analog color-phase behavior needs the composite model.

name: Andor 1
reason: Ordinary media playback is feasible; exact format support and legacy quirks have not been audited.
